chapter: Studio recordings of the late twenties and thirties
title: Harlem Twist, his vocal, and unissued records
summary: Kline asks about Harlem Twist with Red Nichols, on which Morehouse sang; Morehouse keeps humming Three Blind Mice and notes some records never came out.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I'm going to ask you, I don't know whether you remember this or not Chauncey, one of the Red Nichols records you made, you did the vocal.
Oh you wrote that? Oh do you remember how that goes?
Let me ask you again, okay. 'Three Blind Mice' was your best known song.
Okay. This was a song called 'Harlem Twist'.
Right. Do you remember that song?
Well it must be down here somewhere.
All I know is it's right there, "Harlem Twist". That's all I know about it. And you did the vocal on the record. Do you remember that.
Nichols, McConville, Moll, Fosdick, Schutt, Fud Livingston, Jimmy Dorsey, Schutt, Kress, Chauncey Morehouse, drums, the vibes and vocal.
Do you remember that song, "Harlem Twist?"
You see, some of these things didn't come out.
You mean some of the records didn't come out.
Some of the records didn't come out.
They never issued some of the records.
I wish they would. A lot of records, they didn't issue back, you know in the old days, they've reissued as LPs.
So some of them may still be coming out for the first time.
